text: Automatically reviews every pull request with full understanding of the whole codebase
quote: Greptile is an AI code review agent that automatically reviews every pull request with complete understanding of your codebase.

text: Review comments include a 'Fix with your Agent' button that sends the issue with file/line context to Claude Code, Codex, Conductor, Cursor, or Devin
quote: Every review comment includes a Fix with your Agent button that sends the issue — with file paths, line numbers, and suggested code — straight to Claude Code, Codex, Conductor, Cursor, or Devin.

text: A 'Fix All' button sends every flagged issue in a review to the agent at once
quote: A Fix All button in the review summary sends every issue at once.

text: Thumbs up/down reactions and replies teach the reviewer what to stop flagging over time
quote: Your 👍/👎 reactions and replies teach Greptile what matters. After 2-3 weeks, it stops commenting on things you don't care about.

text: Installs by connecting GitHub or GitLab and gives automated PR feedback within minutes of setup
quote: Set up Greptile AI code reviews in 5 minutes. Connect GitHub or GitLab, configure review triggers, and get automated feedback on your first pull request.

text: Official CLI (`greptile onboard`) can set up the product from the terminal, usable by a coding agent
quote: Set up Greptile from your terminal with `greptile onboard` — or hand this page to your coding agent and have it run the setup for you.

text: Can be self-hosted via Docker Compose in your own AWS/GCP/Azure/air-gapped infrastructure with custom LLM configs
quote: Deploy Greptile in your own infrastructure with Docker Compose. Supports AWS, GCP, Azure, air-gapped environments, and custom LLM configurations.

text: Self-hosted deployment scales from single-VM Docker Compose (up to 100 devs) to Kubernetes (100+ devs, HA)
quote: Docker Compose: Up to 100 developers. Single VM, simpler operations. Kubernetes: 100+ developers. Horizontal scaling, high availability.

text: Requires allowlisting Greptile's IP range if GitHub/GitLab restricts inbound traffic
quote: If your GitHub or GitLab instance restricts inbound traffic to specific IP addresses, you need to allowlist Greptile's IP range for code review to work.

text: Any coding agent can be launched in one click from a review comment with full context and suggested fix
quote: Launch any agent in one click with a Greptile comment, full context, and suggested fix.

text: Review comments, fixes, and coding patterns can be accessed and managed directly from your coding agent
quote: Access Greptile review comments, apply fixes, and manage coding patterns directly from your agent of choice.

text: Review comments can be viewed and resolved directly inside Claude Code
quote: View and resolve review comments directly from Claude Code.

text: Supports iterating on a PR until the reviewer gives a perfect score with zero unresolved comments
quote: Iteratively fix a PR until Greptile gives a perfect review: 5/5 confidence, zero unresolved comments.

text: CLI command reviews the feature branch diff and returns results in about 60 seconds
quote: Run `greptile review`, get a review of the feature branch diff in 60 seconds.

text: Coding agents themselves can invoke the Greptile CLI to review their own generated code
quote: Coding agents can use the greptile cli to review their own code

text: Gives each PR a 0-5 merge-safety confidence score
quote: Know how safe a PR is to merge at a glance with a 0-5 score

text: Generates sequence diagrams and flowcharts to help explain complex PR changes
quote: Parse complex changes with sequence diagrams and flowcharts generated for every PR

text: Automatically generates unit tests for new or changed code in a PR
quote: Automatically generate unit tests for new and changed code in every PR

text: TREX runs the PR branch in a sandbox, exercising services and UI flows to catch runtime-only bugs, attaching logs/screenshots/traces
quote: TREX runs your PR branch in a sandbox to find the bugs that only show up at runtime. It starts services, mocks inputs, clicks through UI flows, and leaves the logs, screenshots, and traces on the PR.

text: A strictness setting (1-3) controls how aggressively the reviewer leaves comments
quote: Control how strict Greptile is about leaving comments with the strictness setting (1–3).

text: Supports creating custom rules to catch team-specific issues
quote: Create custom rules that catch team-specific issues

text: A `greptile.json` file in the repo root configures review settings, overriding dashboard defaults
quote: Place `greptile.json` in your repository root. Settings are read from the source branch of the PR and override dashboard settings.

text: Can fetch unaddressed review feedback for any PR via CLI/tooling
quote: Fetch PR comments - Get unaddressed Greptile feedback for any PR

text: Cursor, Claude Code, VS Code, and Codex can connect to Greptile via an official MCP server with OAuth
quote: Connect Cursor, Claude Code, VS Code, or Codex to Greptile MCP with OAuth.

text: Combines static scanning with an AI security agent to catch vulnerabilities in every PR
quote: Greptile pairs static scanning with an AI security agent to catch vulnerabilities in every pull request.

text: v5 runs a swarm of narrowly scoped agents in parallel for faster reviews, more bugs caught, fewer false positives
quote: v5 is faster, catches more bugs, and flags fewer false positives by running a swarm of narrowly scoped agents in parallel.

text: Detects when a PR was authored by a coding agent and routes review to a different model (e.g., GPT reviews Claude-written code)
quote: Greptile can now detect when a PR was authored by a coding agent and route the review to a different model. If Claude wrote it, GPT reviews it, and if GPT wrote it, Claude reviews it.

text: Self-hosted deployments run in the customer's own VPC and can also self-host the LLMs used for review
